questions.question_text: What is the primary purpose of maintaining a 'Diary Register' in a government or corporate office?
options: To track incoming dak and correspondence received
questions.explanation: A diary register is used to systematically record all incoming letters, files, and correspondence received in an office to ensure accountability and tracking.

questions.question_text: In noting and drafting, what term is used for a temporary file or note sheet used to record interim decisions before final approval?
questions.explanation: A note is recorded on the note sheet of a file by officers and staff to analyze the case, cite precedents, and propose a course of action.

questions.question_text: Which type of communication is generally used for correspondence between two government ministries or departments on a personal level between officers?
questions.explanation: A Demi-Official (DO) letter is used for correspondence between government officers when personal attention of the recipient is desired or when expedition is required.

questions.question_text: What does 'PUC' stand for in official file management terminology?
questions.explanation: PUC stands for Paper Under Consideration, which refers to the main letter, document, or reference upon which action is being taken in the file.

questions.question_text: When a file is closed and stored away permanently or for a long term due to completion of action, what is it called?
questions.explanation: Recording a file means the process of closing a file after all actions are complete and indexing/storing it systematically in the record room.

questions.question_text: What is the primary action taken when a physical dak (mail) is received in an office registry section?
options: It is immediately shredded if confidential
It is entered into the Dispatch Register
It is entered into the Diary Register with a unique serial number
It is sent directly to the archives
questions.explanation: The Diary Register is used to record all incoming mail/dak with a distinct serial number for tracking purposes.

questions.question_text: In office file management, what does 'Index Slip' refer to?
options: A slip used for marking attendance
A reference card or slip containing catchwords to help trace a file easily
A financial statement attached to bills
A note sheet indicating urgent delivery
questions.explanation: Index slips contain subject keywords and file numbers to facilitate quick retrieval of archived or running files.

questions.question_text: Which of the following describes an 'Endorsement' on an official document or letter?
options: A financial audit report attached at the end
A statement written or stamped on a document directing it to another authority for information or action
The final signature of the head of the department
The rejection slip of a tender proposal
questions.explanation: An endorsement is used when a copy of a communication is forwarded to other offices or officers for information or necessary action.

questions.question_text: What is the primary objective of weeding out old files in an office?
options: To reduce clutter and free up storage space by destroying useless records
To create extra noting space in current files
To increase the count of active files
questions.explanation: Weeding out refers to the systematic review and destruction of files whose retention period has expired.

questions.question_text: When a file is sent outside the department, which register must be updated to track its movement?
questions.explanation: The Dispatch Register records all outgoing letters, files, and documents sent outside the organization or department.

questions.question_text: What is meant by the term 'Demi-Official (D.O.) Letter'?
options: A personal correspondence between government officers of equivalent or higher rank on official matters
A public notice published in the newspaper
A memorandum issued to junior staff for misconduct
questions.explanation: A D.O. letter is addressed by name to an officer to draw personal attention to urgent or confidential official matters.

questions.question_text: In government noting, who is responsible for initiating the note on a newly received paper or file?
questions.explanation: The dealing assistant examines the receipt, checks previous papers, and records the initial note on the note sheet.

questions.question_text: What does a 'Reminder' signify in official correspondence?
options: An alarm set on office computers
A follow-up communication sent when no reply has been received within a stipulated time
A penalty notice for late attendance
questions.explanation: Reminders are issued to expedite replies or actions on pending references.

questions.question_text: Which part of a file contains the chronological record of all discussions, decisions, and orders passed?
questions.explanation: The note sheet forms the left side or distinct section of the file where deliberations and noting take place chronologically.

questions.question_text: What is the purpose of a 'Stock Register' in an office?
options: To record the daily attendance of employees
To keep an inventory of non-consumable and durable assets/goods purchased
To track daily inward postal charges
questions.explanation: Stock registers maintain a permanent record of permanent or semi-permanent office furniture, equipment, and machinery.
